newsitem.title: FRANCE: British beef embargo to stay after mad cow data-EU.
newsitem.headline: British beef embargo to stay after mad cow data-EU.

text.p: The European Union will maintain an embargo on British beef exports after scientists found more evidence the cattle disease could spread to people, Agriculture Commissioner Franz Fischler said on Thursday.

"What the British scientists have discovered shows how serious the crisis is," he told a news conference. "We must make sure all the measures which have been put in place are maintained, because now we have to face the fact that the disease can be transmitted to people."

The research published on Wednesday found that a new variant of fatal Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) in humans left traces very similar to the brain-wasting cattle disease, known scientifically as bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE).

"(The research) shows that the risk of transmission to humans is a fact -- it is not the proof, but it is one more proof," Fischler said after briefing a French parliamentary committee on the seven-month-old European beef crisis.
Speaking in German through a French translator, Austrian-born Fischler said the evidence reinforced the need for an eradication plan agreed by EU leaders this summer to be fully implemented.
"It demonstrates that the measures agreed between Britain and other states must be maintained," Fischler said.
The EU banned British beef exports in March after London first reported a suspected link between mad cow disease and CJD.
At a summit in June, EU leaders agreed on a series of steps Britain must take to get the global export ban lifted, including an accelerated slaughter programme of 147,000 cattle.
But London put the additional cull on hold last month after experts said it would not speed up the disappearance of BSE.
Fischler told reporters in Paris that the cull was a pre-condition for the export ban to be eased.
British Prime Minister John Major insisted earlier on Thursday that meat from British cattle was safe to eat despite the latest findings.
He told BBC Television there was no justification for the EU to harden its stance against lifting the export ban.
